content: Sodium hypophosphite (NaPO2H2) is the sodium salt derived from hypophosphorous acid. At room temperature, it exists as a solid in the form of odorless white crystals. This compound is water-soluble and has a hygroscopic nature, meaning it readily absorbs moisture from the surrounding air. It is essential to store sodium hypophosphite in a cool, dry environment, away from oxidizing agents, to maintain its stability and prevent unwanted reactions. When exposed to heat, sodium hypophosphite decomposes and releases toxic phosphine gas, which can irritate the respiratory system. Proper precautions should be taken to avoid inhalation of this gas during handling or heating. Sodium hypophosphite is primarily utilized in electroless nickel plating, a process that allows the formation of a durable nickel-phosphorus coating on objects, including those with irregular surfaces. This technique is widely applied in industries such as electronics, aviation, and petroleum. Additionally, sodium hypophosphite can serve as a food additive, as specified in regulations effective from November 17, 2001, which also include other salts of hypophosphorous acid.
